issue_context.title: move GetKernelVersion out of `pkg/proxy/ipvs`
issue_context.body:
The ipvs proxy has code to check the kernel version (including a mockable interface), and this has ended up getting used outside of that code; currently in kubelet (`pkg/kubelet/sysctl`) for figuring out what sysctls are available (for pods to request to be set), and in the future in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120354, for figuring out if a certain conntrack hack is needed.

We should move that code somewhere more generic.

/sig network
/cc @aroradaman @cyclinder

That sounds great, but the changed code still needs to be accessible by the kubelet, because we need the kubelet to decide if the pods with safe sysctl are working properly or not

I think we should move this to https://github.com/kubernetes/utils Or https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/version/version.go, After the move is complete, We update all code in k/k (such as kubelet and kube-proxy) that uses `GetKernelVersion` so that they no longer import ipvs packages.

/assign
I thought of k/utils and k/k/pkg/util but couldn't find any relevant package and we already import **sysctl** from k/component-helpers/node/util in kube-proxy

Most of the time, If we use `GetKernelVersion`, we should import https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/version/version.go, which has some version comparison functions.

If it's only shared between kubelet and kube-proxy it doesn't need to be in `staging`; it can just be in `pkg/util` somewhere. (I'm not saying component-helpers or whatever is definitely wrong, but usually we don't put things there until it's needed by something outside of core...)

> Most of the time, If we use `GetKernelVersion`, we should import https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/version/version.go, which has some version comparison functions.

Yes, adding some additional helper functions based on the existing users could be useful.

@danwinship do we still need the mockable interface ?
Right now there is no mocked implementation of `KernelHandler`, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111806 removed the `fakeKernelHandler` and this consumed as a utility function only. Will a simple utility function be sufficient  ?

review_comments: I don't think we need these new files, as mentioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120895#issuecomment-1736792795, it's nice that we just added extra functions in `pkg/util/version.go`, In this way, for most users, they do not need to import/change additional package (they have already imported pkg/util/version)

> Most of the time, If we use GetKernelVersion, we should import https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/version/version.go, which has some version comparison functions.

I don't think that is the right place for this, `staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/version` provides utilities for version number comparisons not for fetching versions for a source.

We definitely need comparable kernel version that is why I'm parsing kernel version string and returning kernel version as a *version.Version object.

The callers can directly use `version.MustParseGeneric` on the version string to compare with 🙂 
```go
kernelVersion.LessThan(version.MustParseGeneric(utilkernel.IPVSConnReuseModeMinSupportedKernelVersion))
```
I prefer to move these variables to `version.go`, they are associative and easy to understand
I'm not sure these belong in a central place, really.  Fine for now, but seems kind of dirty

So after suggesting that you should move these constants here, it occurred to me that maybe this is a bad idea because it means that every time we add a new kernel version constraint to the ipvs proxier, we'll need to add a new constant here and then get a `pkg/` approver to approve the PR.

we can, if we think that's appropriate... I guess nobody else is likely to be fiddling with sysctls...

In this case, If we move `GetKernelVersion` from `proxy/ipvs` to `pkg/util/version`, We can only import `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/version`, and we don't need to import any additional package, It's good for users.
`k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/version` is not about _specific_ software, it's just about parsing version numbers in general. It's used in lots of places that don't care about the kernel at all.
